questions.question: Explain the event loop in JavaScript and how asynchronous callbacks are processed.
questions.expectedAnswer: The event loop monitors the Call Stack and the Task Queue (Callback Queue and Microtask Queue). When the call stack is empty, it pushes tasks from queues to the stack, prioritizing microtasks like Promises over macrotasks like setTimeout.
questions.explanation: JavaScript is single-threaded. Concurrency is achieved through the browser/Node event loop coordinating the V8 engine, Web APIs, and queue mechanisms.
keyPoints: Macrotasks (setTimeout, setInterval, I/O) execute after microtask drain

questions.question: Two Sum Problem: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target.
questions.expectedAnswer: Use a hash map to store previously seen numbers and their indices. For each number x, check if (target - x) exists in the hash map. This achieves O(n) time and O(n) space complexity.
questions.explanation: Brute force checks all pairs in O(n^2). Storing complements in a dictionary reduces lookup time to O(1) on average.
keyPoints: O(n) time complexity, O(n) auxiliary space
Edge case handling: duplicate numbers, no solution

codingDetails.problemStatement: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target. You may assume that each input would have exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.
codingDetails.constraints:
2 <= nums.length <= 10^4
-10^9 <= nums[i] <= 10^9
-10^9 <= target <= 10^9
Only one valid answer exists.
codingDetails.example:
Input: nums = [2, 7, 11, 15], target = 9
Output: [0, 1]
Explanation: Because nums[0] + nums[1] == 9, we return [0, 1].
codingDetails.expectedApproach: Iterate through the array while maintaining a hash table mapping each element value to its index. At index i, compute complement = target - nums[i]. If complement is in the map, return [map[complement], i]. Otherwise, record nums[i]: i.
codingDetails.solutionExplanation: Time Complexity: O(n) where n is the number of elements. Space Complexity: O(n) for the hash map.

questions.question: What are the main principles of RESTful API design and how do HTTP status codes reflect operation results?
questions.expectedAnswer: REST principles include client-server separation, statelessness, cacheability, uniform interface, and layered systems. HTTP verbs (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH) represent actions, while status codes (2xx success, 3xx redirection, 4xx client errors, 5xx server errors) inform the client of outcomes.
questions.explanation: Adhering to standard HTTP semantics allows predictable client consumption and reliable distributed caching.
keyPoints: Stateless communication where every request contains all necessary auth and data
Resource-oriented URI naming with proper HTTP methods

questions.question: Explain the event loop in JavaScript and how asynchronous callbacks are processed.
questions.userAnswer: The event loop in JavaScript allows non-blocking execution by managing call stack and queues. Synchronous code runs on the call stack. Asynchronous callbacks from timers or fetch go to queues. Microtasks like promises execute first when stack clears, followed by macrotasks.

evaluation.strengths: Clearly distinguished microtasks vs macrotasks and call stack processing.
evaluation.missingPoints: Could mention libuv in Node or Web APIs in browser.
evaluation.suggestions: Mentioning event loop starvation or long-running CPU blocking adds extra depth.
evaluation.idealAnswer: The event loop monitors Call Stack and queues. When Call Stack empties, it flushes microtask queue (Promises) before picking the next macrotask (setTimeout).
